topic_summary: Analysis of Turkey's 1928 alphabet reform (Law 1353), which replaced Arabic script with Latin script for Turkish within months via top-down decree. The reform had effectively zero pre-existing Latin-script practitioners, making it a test case for whether a contested kernel (script-as-identity) can be installed with no prior occupancy of the new reading—a 'clean slate' imposition that bypasses gradual drift.

key_entities: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (reform architect; secular modernization authority)
Ottoman Empire (defunct polity; Arabic-script legacy holder)
Turkish Grand National Assembly (legislative body; ratified Law 1353)
Arabic script (Ottoman administrative/religious medium; 600+ year incumbent)
Latin script (imposed replacement; zero prior Turkish practitioners)
key_tensions: Secular modernization vs Islamic continuity (Kemalist state vs Ottoman religious identity)
Literacy accessibility vs cultural rupture (phonetic transparency vs historical text access)
State sovereignty vs imperial legacy (Republic vs Ottoman institutional memory)
key_mechanisms: Legal prohibition: Arabic script banned for public use within 3 months (enforcement via fines/closure)
Mass literacy campaigns: 'Nation Schools' program teaching Latin script to adults
Textual erasure: All government documents, street signs, educational materials reissued
Authority re-grounding: Script change severs institutional continuity with Ottoman past
key_absences: No documented resistance movement: lack of organized opposition despite cultural magnitude
No transition period: immediate switch vs gradual digraphia (cf. Soviet Turkic reforms)
No preservation infrastructure: pre-1928 texts became inaccessible to new generations

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Script-as-identity: the shared substrate that written language encodes and transmits communal memory, religious authority, and legitimate governance
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Post-Ottoman Turkish state claims exclusive authority to define national identity via script selection, grounding legitimacy in modernization rather than continuity

readings.commitment: Arabic script is constitutive of Turkish-Islamic identity and historical continuity
readings.expected_structural_delta: High suppression cost; script preserves access to Ottoman institutional memory; religious authority structure maintained

readings.commitment: Latin script enables secular modernization by severing Ottoman-Islamic past
readings.expected_structural_delta: Zero transition cost (no incumbents to displace); textual rupture is feature not bug; state monopolizes literacy apparatus

readings.commitment: Script is neutral technology; Latin provides superior phonetic transparency for Turkish vowel harmony
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low ε (technical optimization); depoliticizes decision; obscures identity-encoding function

axiom_contradictions.basis: Continuity reading holds that legitimate authority derives from preserving historical identity substrate; rupture reading holds that legitimate authority derives from severing that substrate. No framework can simultaneously ground authority in both preservation and erasure of the same identity kernel.

axes.primary_observable: Accessibility of pre-1928 texts to post-reform population; religious authority structure continuity
axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading 1 of 3: represents incumbent constraint (Arabic script as identity substrate); high ε due to suppression cost of 600-year precedent

axes.selection_reason: Kernel reading 2 of 3: represents imposed constraint (zero-occupancy installation); highest centrality due to state enforcement mechanism; axiom-contradictory with ottoman_continuity_reading

axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream consequence of rupture reading rather than independent constraint; captured by phonetic_instrumentalism_reading's technical framing

omegas.description: Does the absence of pre-existing Latin-script practitioners mean the reform bypassed M-set conflict entirely, or did it merely suppress latent Ottoman-continuity commitment that lacked organizational capacity? If the latter, the 'clean slate' is artifact of state coercion rather than genuine kernel vacancy.
omegas.source: Research context flag: M-set gap claim requires validation against absence of documented resistance

omegas.description: Is phonetic_instrumentalism_reading a genuine constraint (linguistic community held this as primary justification) or post-hoc legitimation scaffold for political rupture? If the latter, it is not a true kernel reading but rather rhetorical cover for snare extraction.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan): technical framing benefits state by depoliticizing identity contest

omegas.description: The absence of documented resistance may reflect successful state suppression rather than genuine absence of opposition. If archival silence is coerced rather than consensual, the 'zero practitioner' framing is state propaganda rather than structural fact.
omegas.source: Extraction absence inventory: no recorded resistance movement despite cultural magnitude

omegas.description: Would gradual transition (temporary digraphia, as in Soviet Turkic reforms) have revealed latent continuity-reading holders? The immediate switch may have foreclosed observation of the M-set structure by eliminating the transition period where competing readings would visibly coexist.
omegas.source: Extraction absence inventory: no transition period; comparison to Soviet gradual reforms
